title: Yarrow infusion for fever support
subtitle: A traditional diaphoretic infusion for mild fever
excerpt: A hot infusion of dried yarrow aerial parts, taken warm at 1-2 teaspoons per cup. Traditionally used to encourage gentle perspiration during a mild fever, as part of the body's own response. For mild fever in adults only . not for high fever, febrile convulsions, or children under two.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), Yarrow (Achillea millefolium) entry : diaphoretic use in fevers. King's American Dispensatory (Felter and Lloyd, 1898), Achillea section. Traditional western herbal diaphoretic use for mild self-limiting fever.

glossaryTerms.definition: A herb traditionally used to encourage gentle perspiration, associated in western herbal practice with supporting the body's own fever response.

content.text: Yarrow infusion for fever is a hot-water preparation of dried yarrow aerial parts, taken warm rather than cool. Traditionally described as a

herb, yarrow is one that western herbalists associate with encouraging gentle perspiration and supporting the body's own response to mild fever. One to two teaspoons of dried aerial parts per cup, steeped covered for ten minutes and drunk warm. This remedy is for mild, self-limiting fever in adults only.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body:
Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor for ongoing or serious symptoms.

This remedy is for mild fever in adults only. Do not use for high fever, febrile convulsions, any fever in a child under two years old, or any fever with stiff neck. Seek emergency care immediately for fever with stiff neck, rash, confusion, difficulty breathing, or any infant under three months with any elevated temperature.

Yarrow is in the Asteraceae (daisy) family. Readers with a known allergy to ragweed, daisies, or chamomile should avoid this preparation.

In rare cases, yarrow can increase skin sensitivity to sunlight.

Consult a herbalist or your midwife before using this remedy in pregnancy. Yarrow has traditional traditionally used to ease menstrual cramping (uterine-stimulating) properties and is avoided at therapeutic doses in pregnancy.

Paediatric use is not adult-divided-by-half. Consult a herbalist who specialises in children's herbal medicine before using any herbal preparation in children under twelve.

content.text: Bring fresh cold water to the boil, then set aside for one minute.
Place 1-2 teaspoons of dried yarrow in a teapot or cup with a tea infuser. Pour 200 ml of just-off-boil water over the herb and cover immediately.
Steep covered for 10 minutes. The water should turn a pale yellow-green.
Strain and drink warm. Staying warm after drinking is part of the traditional preparation; getting into bed with a blanket is the classical approach.
One cup (1-2 teaspoons of dried herb per 200 ml), up to three times a day while the fever is present. Use for up to three days. If the fever has not resolved within three days, see your doctor.
Dried herb stores for up to 12 months in a sealed tin away from light and moisture. Prepare each cup fresh; do not store the prepared infusion.
When not to use this remedy
Seek emergency care immediately for fever in any infant under three months. Fever with a stiff neck or rash, fever with confusion or difficulty breathing, or any sign of febrile convulsion.
See a doctor if symptoms last more than ten days, temperature rises above 39°C, breathing is laboured, or symptoms worsen after at first improving.
